PMID:28492155.setting: Department of Radiology, Jinnah Hospital, Lahore (tertiary care hospital)
PMID:28492155.standard: American College of Radiology (ACR) recommendations for knee MRI image acquisition

cycle1.result: All three planes acquired; sagittal and coronal slice thickness, gap and coverage appropriate in all. FOV appropriate in 66% axial, 5% sagittal, 0% coronal; adequate axial superior coverage in 13 (66%) and inferior coverage in 16 (80%).

PMID:28492155.intervention: Recommendations (decrease FOV in all planes, increase axial anatomical coverage) presented in departmental meetings.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3426014.setting: Obstetric unit (Medical School, Newcastle University affiliation); cases from birth register and incident reports
EPMC:PMC:PMC3426014.standard: Clinical Negligence Scheme for Trusts (CNST) minimum documentation standards for shoulder dystocia

cycle1.result: All areas 100% documented; brachial plexus injury rate 6.7%.

cycle2.result: Documentation declined: only 65% recorded manoeuvres, timing and stage of delivery; 41% recorded staff attending and time of arrival; sequence of manoeuvres and who performed them not routinely recorded. Brachial plexus injury rate 15.8%.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3426014.other_findings: McRoberts resolved 50% of cases; suprapubic pressure 14%, entry manoeuvres 18%, posterior arm removal 18%. Authors recommend updating the pro forma and restarting skill drills.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8135796.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Bristol Royal Children's Hospital (tertiary referral centre); clinic and theatre data

cycle1.result: AFC and fracture clinic follow-up bookings fell by 40% and 48%; patient-initiated follow-up rose from 16% to 75% (AFC) and 12% to 35% (FFO); only 17% of AFC and 39% of FFO patients needed radiographs; on-call referrals and trauma cases fell by 50%; all elective operating cancelled.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8135796.other_findings: A virtual fracture clinic was implemented with an increasing trend in use.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524492.setting: Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Hospital, Oswestry (orthopaedic surgery)
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524492.standard: Royal College of Surgeons COVID-19 consent guidance: all patients informed of COVID-19 risk (in-hospital risk 0.45%)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 risk documented on 44% of consent forms (56% not documented). Of forms without it, 34% completed by consultants, 18% fellows, 48% registrars.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524492.other_findings: 6% of patients were suspected of COVID post-operatively and tested; 0% contracted COVID.

PMID:22385529.topic: Spinal imaging provision for trauma and tumour
PMID:22385529.setting: 34 public hospitals in Ireland; Emergency Departments and/or orthopaedic registrars questioned

cycle1.result: 67.64% of centres routinely used a spinal clearance protocol; ED cleared the spine in 87%; CT available in hours in 85.3%, out of hours 47%; MRI available in 50%, out of hours in only two centres.

PMID:22385529.other_findings: Questionnaire-based survey of service provision; all centres participated.

PMID:16753088.setting: Hospital ambulatory care in two public hospitals; records reviewed by two rehabilitation doctors
PMID:16753088.standard: Quality indicators developed from systematic reviews, guidelines and expert criteria (history, examination, diagnosis, treatment)

cycle1.result: 76.3% of records did not meet at least 4 of 10 history criteria; 61.6% did not meet at least 3 of 10 examination criteria; 7.7% had no diagnosis. 96.9% of 98 impingement patients did not meet anti-inflammatory/injection timing criteria; 95.8% of 24 rotator cuff tears not proposed for early surgical evaluation; 86.7% of 15 adhesive capsulitis cases lacked timely exercise instructions.

PMID:16753088.other_findings: Up to 15.3% of impingement patients were not offered physiotherapy or exercise within 4 weeks; poor record quality may explain part of the deficit.

PMID:29169299.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit (national, MSK Audit group)

cycle1.result: Male proportion rose from 22.4% to 29.5% (p < 0.0001); admission from own home rose from 63.9% to 73.1% (p < 0.0001); ASA grade 3 rose from 52.9% to 56.4%.

PMID:29169299.other_findings: Registry report of demographics only; audit discontinued in 2008 and recommenced in 2013.

PMID:31155894.setting: Aintree University Hospital, Liverpool (major trauma centre); image intensifier films reviewed on PACS by at least two blinded observers
PMID:31155894.standard: Reduction criteria published by Pettrone et al.

cycle1.result: Malreduction rate 33%.

PMID:31155894.intervention: Education and reflection between 2013 and 2015; then a change in process in ankle fracture management supported by education between 2015 and 2017.
PMID:31155894.other_findings: Interim 2015 re-audit (68 patients, after education alone) showed malreduction rising to 43.8%. Final major complication rate 0.98%; deep infection 0.5%.

PMID:9861924.setting: Department of Paediatric Orthopaedics, Starship Children's Hospital, Auckland

cycle1.result: MRI correlated well for spinal, congenital, intra-articular and growth plate pathology; 3/10 (30%) foreign body assessments incorrect (sensitivity 0.60, specificity 0.80); 3/20 (15%) could not distinguish oedema/effusion from infection (sensitivity 1.00, specificity 0.73); 4/27 soft tissue tumours did not correlate with histology (sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.63).

PMID:9861924.other_findings: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy review; MRI accurate for tumour margins and extent.

PMID:19185658.setting: Royal College of Radiologists national audit of NHS MRI services
PMID:19185658.standard: RCR standards for MRI provision: request-to-report times and recommended waiting times for cancer staging and routine orthopaedic examinations

cycle1.result: Request-to-report time did not meet the standard for cancer staging but was within target for routine orthopaedic examinations nationally; mean waiting times longer than recommended for both.

PMID:19185658.intervention: Major investment in MRI capacity: new NHS scanners and, in England, outsourcing of routine MRI to an independent provider.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in waiting times for routine orthopaedic examinations; cancer staging examinations deteriorated.

PMID:19185658.other_findings: Control charts showed underperformance due to common cause variation, needing whole-process improvement from request to report.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524610.setting: Single orthopaedic unit (University of Glasgow affiliation); emergency and elective consent forms
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524610.standard: Best practice for informed consent: patients made aware of risk of contracting COVID-19

cycle1.result: COVID-19 included as a risk in 21/51 (41.2%); elective 10/24 (41.7%), emergency 11/27 (40.7%).

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524610.intervention: Results circulated to all orthopaedic staff as a poster, with 2 weeks of educational awareness.
EPMC:PMC:PMC8524610.other_findings: Elective practice remained poor. One patient tested positive pre-operatively and one post-operatively.

PMID:24651138.topic: Tibial stress fracture screening and management
PMID:24651138.setting: Outpatient clinic, US Army setting (Martin Army Community Hospital, Fort Benning)
PMID:24651138.standard: Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm

cycle1.result: 16 tibial stress fractures diagnosed.

PMID:24651138.intervention: Implementation of the Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm for lower leg pain.

cycle2.result: 30 tibial stress fractures diagnosed (87.5% increase); provider adherence to LPS&RT 93.3% on chart audit.

PMID:24651138.other_findings: Common treatments were activity restriction, oral medication and specialty referral; 46 patients in total.

PMID:35320180.setting: Surgical Oncology Department, Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Pre-operative ASIA grade E in 8 (50%); post-operative grade E in 14 (87.5%); 1 (6.25%) wound infection.

PMID:35320180.other_findings: Breast was the commonest primary (62.5%) and lumbar spine most involved (62.5%).

PMID:22647555.setting: NHS orthopaedic department before and after appointment of a podiatric surgeon

cycle1.result: Questionnaires returned by 56/88 (63.6%) podiatric and 60/88 (68.2%) orthopaedic patients. Satisfaction excellent 63.7%, moderate/good 23.6%, poor 12.7% (podiatric) vs excellent 43.4%, moderate 17%, poor 39.6% (orthopaedic).

PMID:22647555.other_findings: Satisfaction survey with labour force implications; patients matched by OPCS code.

PMID:15648710.setting: District General Orthopaedic Unit, The Ayr Hospital; allograft from primary joint arthroplasty for West of Scotland Blood Transfusion Service

cycle1.result: Allograft not collected from 22/70 suitable patients; 68.6% of suitable bone collected. 29% of donated allograft rejected due to poor patient selection.

PMID:15648710.intervention: Procedural changes to improve the efficiency of allograft collection (not detailed).

cycle2.result: 8/70 allografts discarded due to logistical problems; 88.9% of suitable allograft collected (p = 0.001). Rejection for poor selection fell to 9.4% (p = 0.05).

PMID:15648710.other_findings: Medical contraindications excluded 8/80 in cycle 1 and 28/100 in cycle 2.

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383599.setting: Emergency department, TUH (Tallaght University Hospital), proximal femoral fractures
EPMC:PMC:PMC9383599.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of ED attendance

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% of patients reached ward (within standard).

EPMC:PMC:PMC9383599.intervention: 90-minute multidisciplinary simulation training on the hip fracture pathway for ED staff (32 people; in person and via Zoom), February 2021.

cycle2.result: Not reported in abstract (text truncated); authors conclude improved time to ward and compliance with IHFS 1.

PMID:27652791.setting: Fracture clinic, district general hospital (Croydon Health Services NHS Trust)
PMID:27652791.standard: British Orthopaedic Association: patients referred to fracture clinic reviewed within 72 hours

cycle1.result: Mean waiting time 10.7 days; 6% seen within 72 hours.

PMID:27652791.intervention: Virtual fracture clinic introduced for all ED referrals to fracture clinic.

cycle2.result: All patients reviewed within 72 hours (mean 1.3 days).

PMID:27652791.other_findings: Achieved with no increase in clinic capacity and negligible cost.

PMID:16721282.topic: Blood cross-match ordering for elective surgery
PMID:16721282.setting: Spinal surgery department, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth; elective lumbar spine operations excluding deformity
PMID:16721282.standard: Evidence-based cross-match tariff (cross-match to transfusion ratio and transfusion index)

cycle1.result: 664 cross-match requests, 40 units transfused; C:T ratio 16.6:1.

PMID:16721282.intervention: New evidence-based cross-match tariff agreed between surgeons, anaesthetists and transfusion department.

PMID:9038497.topic: VTE prophylaxis in hip and knee surgery
PMID:9038497.setting: Orthopaedic department, St James's University Hospital, Leeds
PMID:9038497.standard: Departmental thromboembolic prophylaxis policy (TED stockings, subcutaneous low-dose heparin, PEP trial inclusion for fractured neck of femur)

cycle1.result: Subcutaneous heparin given in 43% of primary and 14% of revision hip replacements; all knee replacements received heparin but 75% at incorrect dose. Hip fracture: TED stockings 0% to 70%, heparin 0% to 20%, PEP trial inclusion 0% to 20%.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant improvement in subcutaneous heparin and TED stocking use in arthroplasty and in PEP trial inclusion of hip fracture patients.

PMID:23520291.setting: Level 1 trauma centre (Aristotelian University of Thessaloniki affiliation)

cycle1.result: 19 unplanned reoperations: missed syndesmotic injury 9/19 (47%), non-anatomic reduction 6/19 (31%), fixation failure 4/19 (21%).

PMID:23520291.other_findings: Fixation type, surgeon experience, sex and age were not correlated with failure.

PMID:23084512.topic: Hip fracture emergency department care standards
PMID:23084512.setting: Emergency Department (University of Nottingham affiliation); ED Information System records
PMID:23084512.standard: Standards from national policies and evidence-based literature: early analgesia, accurate clinical assessment, prompt transfer to orthopaedic ward

cycle1.result: Good performance on medical assessment; shortfalls in pressure-care assessment, timely ward transfer and pain relief (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:23084512.other_findings: Authors recommend a care bundle for pain relief, pressure care and fast-tracking.

PMID:18430339.setting: Otolaryngology emergency clinic, Medway Maritime Hospital, Gillingham
PMID:18430339.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping guidelines plus legibility, scored with the ANKLe score

cycle1.result: Baseline ANKLe scores for content and legibility (figures not given in abstract); 20 notes from each of 7 SHOs.

PMID:18430339.intervention: Documentation proforma introduced and handwriting advice given.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in content, legibility and overall ANKLe score.

PMID:23276057.setting: Orthopaedic department, The Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
PMID:23276057.standard: NICE VTE prophylaxis guidance (2010): risk assessment before pharmacological prophylaxis and reassessment at 24 hours

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:23276057.intervention: Risk assessment tool attached to drug charts.

cycle2.result: Re-audit showed attaching the tool to drug charts was workable (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:23276057.other_findings: Authors recommend removing 24-hour reassessment from NICE guidance as many patients are high risk.

PMID:16278178.topic: National hip fracture audit and standards
PMID:16278178.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit and national quality assurance authority (national)
PMID:16278178.standard: Scottish evidence-based hip fracture guidelines (1997, updated 2002) and national standards

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:16278178.other_findings: Descriptive report of national audit, guidelines and standards (A&E care, pre-operative delay, multidisciplinary care, audit participation) as a clinical governance framework.

PMID:8980430.setting: Regional vascular referral unit, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford

cycle1.result: 53 primary operations; 3 primary amputations (6%); 11 patients had complications including one death; 81% symptom-free at median 6 months follow-up.

PMID:8980430.other_findings: Case series; no late vascular complications.

EPMC:PMC:PMC6184774.setting: Mona Vale Hospital, metropolitan hospital, Northern Sydney Local Health District
EPMC:PMC:PMC6184774.standard: Agency for Clinical Innovation (ACI) hip fracture minimum standard 2: pain management

cycle1.result: Hourly pain scores on presentation in 82%; nerve blocks used in 35% in ED; 18% reported severe post-operative pain; neuropathic analgesia used in 14%; inappropriate NSAID use in 10%.

EPMC:PMC:PMC6184774.other_findings: Analgesia prescribing varied; team developing a standardised pain pathway.

PMID:39628021.setting: Osteoarthritis Healthy Weight For Life community programme database

cycle1.result: Greater weight loss was associated with greater improvement in knee pain and function; baseline BMI had no effect.

PMID:39628021.other_findings: Patients with more severe baseline pain improved more for the same weight loss.

PMID:35696288.setting: University Hospital Waterford DDH ultrasound screening programme
PMID:35696288.standard: Recommended scan within 6 weeks (stated in results)

cycle1.result: 255 (26%) referred to orthopaedic clinic; only two infants referred on for persistent DDH; no baby scanned within the recommended 6 weeks later presented with dislocation or needed tertiary referral.

PMID:35696288.other_findings: Female majority of nearly 3:1 among referrals; most treated with harness or bracing.

PMID:1902753.topic: Ankle injury management in the emergency department
PMID:1902753.setting: Accident and emergency department, North Tyneside General Hospital (district general hospital)
PMID:1902753.standard: Locally developed ankle injury protocol based on published reports

cycle1.result: 205 (80%) had radiography; 20 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 13 inappropriate fracture clinic referrals.

PMID:1902753.intervention: Introduction of an ankle injury management protocol.

cycle2.result: 186 (70%) had radiography; 66 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 9 inappropriate referrals (53% reduction); protocol completed in 87% of notes.

PMID:1902753.other_findings: 550 patients over four months across both phases.

PMID:32774021.setting: Orthopaedic department, Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Mumbai (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Death rate 0.55 per 100 admissions per year; trauma the commonest cause of admission and death.

PMID:32774021.other_findings: Admissions peaked in the monsoon months (June to August).

PMID:19995491.setting: Department of orthopaedic surgery, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells; hip hemi-arthroplasty
PMID:19995491.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on surgical documentation (33 parameters)

cycle1.result: Handwritten operation reports scored an average of 58.7%.

PMID:19995491.intervention: Procedure-specific computerised operation report proforma for hip hemi-arthroplasty.

cycle2.result: Scores rose significantly (exact figure truncated in abstract).

PMID:19995491.other_findings: Computerised proformas reduced variability between reports.

PMID:15059986.setting: Danish National Indicator Project (all clinical units treating six diseases)
PMID:15059986.standard: Disease-specific clinical indicators and standards (stroke, hip fracture, schizophrenia, acute GI surgery, heart failure, lung cancer)

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:15059986.other_findings: Descriptive paper on mandatory national indicator monitoring with monthly feedback and audit processes.

PMID:17157847.setting: District general hospital (Good Hope Hospital NHS Trust, Birmingham); Austin-Moore hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Re-operation rate 1.4% (3/212) with laminar airflow vs 5.8% (134/223 as printed) in non-laminar theatres.

PMID:17157847.other_findings: Described as a second-cycle audit after introduction of water-impervious gowns and drapes, but reports an outcome comparison only.

PMID:21385830.setting: Single liver transplant centre, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge

cycle1.result: Incident clinical fractures in 15 (3.5%) patients; mean follow-up 61.4 months; median time to fracture 26 months.

PMID:21385830.other_findings: 5.6% had a prior fracture; spine was the commonest site.

PMID:40080706.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
PMID:40080706.setting: UK-wide RCR audit (with RCP and Royal Osteoporosis Society) of CT radiology reporting
PMID:40080706.standard: RCR audit standards for reporting incidental vertebral fragility fractures on CT

cycle1.result: Audit standards not achieved.

PMID:40080706.intervention: A series of interventions (not detailed in abstract).

cycle2.result: Generalised improvement in compliance, including a 6-percentage point increase in moderate/severe VFFs reported.

PMID:40080706.other_findings: Paper models potential morbidity, mortality and cost benefits and highlights onward referral pathways.

PMID:38751271.setting: Civil Hospital, Karachi (public sector); surgeons across surgical units

cycle1.result: Of 249 responding surgeons: 98% ordered full blood count, 69.5% urea and creatinine, 92% viral markers, 78.7% blood glucose, 71.5% cardiac fitness tests.

PMID:38751271.other_findings: Questionnaire-based; only 4 (1.60%) respondents were orthopaedic. Authors call for standard pre-operative protocols.

PMID:11864175.topic: Microbiology specimen requesting in orthopaedic infection
PMID:11864175.setting: Department of orthopaedic surgery, University Hospital Nijmegen; prospective review by two consultant microbiologists
PMID:11864175.standard: Consultant microbiologist appraisal and existing protocol for prosthetic joint revision

cycle1.result: Requests definitely appropriate in 67% and 85% of episodes (two reviewers); collection, handling and transport definitely appropriate in 56% and 73% of requests; 20/98 (20%) surgical specimens yielded a relevant organism.

PMID:11864175.other_findings: No request was judged unjustified; similar errors found in compliance with the prosthetic joint revision protocol.

PMID:36423534.setting: Orthopaedic practice with internal Fracture Liaison Service, Southeastern United States
PMID:36423534.standard: Recommended FLS guidelines: referral of patients meeting age criteria with first fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 5% FLS referrals.

PMID:36423534.intervention: Alert button in the electronic health record prompting surgeons to refer eligible patients to FLS.

PMID:34634024.topic: Dual mobility total hip arthroplasty outcomes

cycle1.result: Mean Harris hip score 33.7 pre-op and 75.9 post-op; one dislocation; mean stay 5.91 days.

PMID:34634024.other_findings: Other complications included wound infection, haematoma and NSTEMI.

PMID:24480498.topic: Pre-operative foot pumps for ankle fractures
PMID:24480498.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery, Mid-Western Regional Hospital, Limerick

cycle1.result: 64 fractures managed with in-cast AV impulse device vs 73 historical controls: median time to surgery, length of stay and surgical site infections all significantly reduced (figures not given in abstract).

PMID:24480498.other_findings: Comparative outcome study of a device.
